newsitem.title: GERMANY: German builders-97 investment to fall real 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: German builders-97 investment to fall real 2.2 pct.

text.p: A German construction industry group said on Friday it expected building investment in 1997 to fall 2.2 percent in real terms.
The Association of the German Construction Industry also said orders for the January-February period were down 7.5 percent in real terms.
German builders-97 investment to fall real 2.2 pct
Investment was expected to decline 1.4 percent in western Germany, and 4.1 percent in eastern Germany, the group said.

In the first two months of 1997, orders in western Germany were down a real 6.9 percent due to a 12.1 percent fall in private business construction. Orders in home and public works construction fell 3.8 percent and 0.8 percent, respectively.

East German orders in January and February dropped 9.2 percent as public construction orders plunged 23.7 percent and business construction dropped 14.6 percent. These were partially offset by a 9.2 percent gain in orders for homes.
The industry employed an average of 1.1 million workers in the two-month period, down 120,000, or 9.7 percent, from the same period in 1996.

For all of 1997, the group said average construction employment was seen falling to 1.2 million, down six percent from the level last year. It expected east German payrolls to decline 9 percent to 380,000 workers, and west German payrolls to fall five percent to 852,000.
